st.2: All but about 75 of its verses are taken from the Yajurveda.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: all but about 75 of its verses come from the Rigveda, not the Yajurveda. Statement 3 is incorrect: its priest is the Udgatri; the Adhvaryu belongs to the Yajurveda.

st.2: Prasenjit of Magadha became a disciple of the Buddha along with his family.
st.1: The Buddhist councils were held at Rajgir, Sravasti, Pataliputra and Kashmir.
st.4: The Buddha spent his last rainy season at Sravasti.

x: All four statements are incorrect. The councils were held at Rajgir, Vaishali, Pataliputra and Kashmir, not Sravasti. Prasenjit ruled Kosala, not Magadha. Udayana ruled Vatsa (Kaushambi), not Avanti. The Buddha spent his last rainy season at Beluva near Vaishali, not Sravasti.

st.2: The Vinaya Pitaka contains five Nikayas.
st.3: The Abhidhamma Pitaka has seven books, from the Dhammasangani to the Milindapanha.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the five Nikayas belong to the Sutta Pitaka, not the Vinaya Pitaka. Statement 3 is incorrect: the seven Abhidhamma books run from the Dhammasangani to the Patthana; the Milindapanha is not one of them. Statement 4 is incorrect: the Khuddaka Nikaya contains about 547 Jatakas.

st.1: Buddhism in Andhra received its greatest royal patronage under the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the greatest royal patronage came under the Ikshvakus of Vijayapuri; the Eastern Chalukyas favoured Brahmanical faiths. Statement 2 is incorrect: Buddhism had royal support in Andhra long before the Vishnukundins (Satavahanas, Ikshvakus).

st.3: Dhanyakataka (Amaravati), linked with Bhavaviveka, was a learning centre under the Satavahanas.

x: All three statements are correct. Nalanda was a Mahayana centre where Dharmakirti taught and was sacked by Bakhtiyar Khalji; Dhanyakataka (Amaravati), linked with Bhavaviveka, flourished under the Satavahanas.

st.1: The sect survived for about 1,000 years.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the Ajivika sect survived for about 2,000 years. Statement 2 is incorrect: it finally disappeared in the 14th century CE from Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, not Bengal and Bihar.

st.2: The Tamil poet Tiruvalluvar refers to the southward push of the Mauryas.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: Bindusara, not Chandragupta Maurya, is regarded as the Mauryan conqueror of the Deccan. Statement 2 is incorrect: it is the Sangam poet Mamulanar, not Tiruvalluvar, who refers to the Mauryan push southward.

st.1: The Dhammayatra to Bodh Gaya was made in the 21st regnal year.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the Dhammayatra to Bodh Gaya was made in the 11th regnal year; the 21st year saw the visit to Lumbini. Statement 2 is incorrect: Dhamma Mahamatras were appointed in the 14th regnal year (RE V). Statement 3 is correct: Rajukas got independent judicial power in the 26th year (PE IV).

st.2: A Samudragupta-period record is found at Sankaram in East Godavari.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: Sankaram lies in the Visakhapatnam (Anakapalli) area, not East Godavari. Statement 3 is incorrect: Avamukta was ruled by Nilaraja; Ugrasena ruled Palakka.

st.2: His gold coins were called dinaras.

x: All three statements are correct. The Udayagiri inscription of Virasena attests the Saka campaign, his gold coins were called dinaras (silver coins were rupakas), and the lion-slayer coins gave him the title Simhavikrama.

st.2: The vishaya was a larger unit than the vithi.

x: All three statements are correct. The vithi, a group of villages headed by the Ayuktaka, was a sub-unit of the larger vishaya, and the grama was headed by the Gramika with the mahattaras.

st.4: The Mandasor inscription showing zero as a circle dates to 876 CE.
st.1: Aryabhata laid down rules for zero and negative numbers and studied cyclic quadrilaterals.
st.3: Bhaskara I wrote decimal numbers with a circle for zero in 729 CE.

x: None of the statements is correct. Brahmagupta, not Aryabhata, gave rules for zero and negative numbers and studied cyclic quadrilaterals. The Khandakhadyaka was written by Brahmagupta, not Aryabhata. Bhaskara I used a circle for zero in 629 CE, not 729 CE. The inscription of 876 CE showing zero as a circle is at Gwalior, not Mandasor.

st.1: Vijayalaya was a Pandya feudatory at Uraiyur before he founded the imperial line.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: Vijayalaya was a Pallava, not Pandya, feudatory. Statement 2 is incorrect: he captured Thanjavur from the Muttaraiyars around 850 CE, not 950 CE.

st.1: A later popular tradition says Kafur obtained it from Ramachandradeva at Devagiri.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the popular tradition links the Koh-i-Noor to Prataparudra at Warangal, not Ramachandradeva at Devagiri. Statement 2 is incorrect: no contemporary record confirms that Kafur obtained it at Warangal.

st.1: Qutbuddin Aibak, the first Sultan, was the slave of Mahmud of Ghazni.
st.4: Ibrahim Lodi, the last Sultan, was killed at Khanwa in 1526.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: Aibak was the slave of Muhammad Ghori, not Mahmud of Ghazni. Statement 3 is incorrect: the first Afghan ruler of Delhi was Bahlol Lodi. Statement 4 is incorrect: Ibrahim Lodi was killed at Panipat in 1526; Khanwa (1527) was fought against Rana Sanga.

st.1: His conversations, the Fawaid-ul-Fuad, were recorded by Amir Hasan Sijzi.

x: All three statements are correct. The Fawaid-ul-Fuad was recorded by Amir Hasan Sijzi; Nizamuddin lived through seven or more reigns without visiting the court, and he left for Ajodhan when Jalaluddin Khalji tried to meet him.

st.3: He took the title 'Padshah' at Samarkand in 1507.
st.1: He was descended from Chingiz Khan on his father's side and from Timur on his mother's side.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: Babur descended from Timur on his father's side and from Chingiz Khan on his mother's side. Statement 2 is incorrect: Chagatai was the second son of Chingiz Khan. Statement 3 is incorrect: he took the title Padshah at Kabul in 1507.

st.3: The revisionist view treats the 18th century as a period of collapse rather than regional growth.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Deccan wars took up roughly the last 25 years of Aurangzeb's reign. Statement 3 is incorrect: the revisionist view sees the 18th century as a period of regional growth, not collapse.

st.1: He bore the titles Kavi Brahma and Ubhaya Kavi Mitrudu.
st.2: His first work, Veerabhadra Vijayam, was written at the request of the Rachakonda king Singabhupala.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: Kavi Brahma and Ubhaya Kavi Mitrudu are Tikkana's titles; Potana was Sahaja Panditudu and Nigarva Chudamani. Statement 2 is incorrect: Veerabhadra Vijayam was written at the request of his guru Ivaturi Somanaradhya. Statement 3 is incorrect: he dedicated the Bhagavatamu to Lord Rama, refusing Singabhupala.

st.3: The Peshwa Daftar was preserved after 1818 by Mountstuart Elphinstone.

x: All three statements are correct. Saranjam was land assigned for military service, and the Peshwa Daftar at Pune, mostly in Modi script, was preserved after 1818 by Mountstuart Elphinstone.

st.1: It was founded in 1664 on the recommendation of Mazarin.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the French East India Company was founded in 1664 on the recommendation of Colbert, not Mazarin. Statement 2 is incorrect: Dupleix was a later Governor-General in India, not its founder.

st.1: Following the Eden Commission (1879), a single Indian Army was formed in 1895 with four commands.

x: All three statements are correct. After the Eden Commission a single Indian Army with four commands was formed in 1895; the Awadh taluqdars became a loyalist class; and English-educated Indians were derided as 'Babus'.

st.1: The Treaty of Masulipatnam was signed in 1788.
st.2: The first Subsidiary Alliance with Hyderabad was made in 1800.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the Treaty of Masulipatnam was signed in 1768. Statement 2 is incorrect: the first Subsidiary Alliance with Hyderabad was made in 1798; the 1800 treaty only expanded it.

st.1: Its story rests mainly on the account of Robert Orme.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the story rests mainly on the account of J.Z. Holwell, not Robert Orme. Statement 2 is incorrect: historians dispute Holwell's numbers.

st.1: Ijaradari meant collecting land revenue through salaried state officials.
st.2: Ijaradari was also called jagirdari.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: Ijaradari meant collecting revenue through contractors (revenue farmers), not salaried officials. Statement 2 is incorrect: it was called mal jasmani, not jagirdari. Statement 4 is incorrect: Murshid Quli Khan, not Mir Jafar, founded the autonomous Bengal Nawabi.

st.3: The Udaipur annexed in 1852 was in Mewar, not Chhattisgarh.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: Dalhousie did not originate the doctrine; lapses had occurred before him (e.g. Mandavi, Kolaba, Jalaun). Statement 3 is incorrect: the Udaipur annexed in 1852 was in Chhattisgarh, not Mewar.

st.3: The Company's request for a government loan in 1772 was followed by Pitt's India Act, 1784.
st.1: After abolishing the Dual Government Warren Hastings shifted the treasury from Calcutta to Murshidabad.

x: None of the statements is correct. Hastings shifted the treasury from Murshidabad to Calcutta, not the other way. Warren Hastings was not the first Governor of Bengal (Robert Clive was); he was the first Governor-General. The loan request of 1772 was followed by the Regulating Act, 1773, not Pitt's India Act.

st.2: The Deccan Riots were associated with peasants' attacks on moneylenders.

x: All three statements are correct. The Pabna movement was a peasant movement, the Deccan Riots (1875) were peasant attacks on moneylenders, and the Rampa Rebellion (1922-24) was led by Alluri Sitarama Raju.

st.2: It was passed in March 1917.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: it was based on the Sedition (Rowlatt) Committee report, not the Lee Commission. Statement 2 is incorrect: it was passed in March 1919.

st.1: He presided over the Congress at Calcutta (1886), Madras (1893) and Calcutta (1906).
st.2: At the Surat session of 1907 he was the first to use 'Swaraj' as the national demand.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: his 1893 presidency was at Lahore, not Madras. Statement 2 is incorrect: he raised 'Swaraj' as the national demand at the Calcutta session of 1906, not Surat 1907. Statement 4 is incorrect: he presided three times, not four.

st.3: The Indian Parliamentary Committee was set up in 1893 by Wedderburn and Charles Bradlaugh.
st.2: The British Committee started the journal 'Young India' in 1890.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the British Committee's journal was 'India', not 'Young India'. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Indian Parliamentary Committee (1893) was set up by Wedderburn and W.S. Caine (Bradlaugh died in 1891). Statement 4 is incorrect: Wedderburn presided over the Bombay session of 1889.

st.2: The Moderates were led by Gokhale and Bipin Chandra Pal.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Moderates were led by Gokhale and Pherozeshah Mehta; Bipin Chandra Pal was an Extremist. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Moderates kept control of the Congress machinery after the split.

st.1: The Bharat Mata Society was active in Punjab under Ajit Singh.

x: All three statements are correct. The Bharat Mata Society worked in Punjab under Ajit Singh, the United Indian Patriotic Association (1888) opposed the Congress, and the first phase of revolutionary nationalism never became a mass movement.

st.4: Most of its passengers were allowed to land at Vancouver despite Canada's 'continuous journey' rule.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: it carried 376 passengers, not 476. Statement 4 is incorrect: almost all its passengers were refused entry under the 'continuous journey' rule and the ship was forced back.

st.3: Ran the secret Congress Radio from Bombay
st.2: Led the Gandhian underground group

st.1: Its first division of 16,300 men was formally raised on 1 September 1943.
st.2: The Tokyo Conference of June 1942 placed the INA under the Indian Independence League.

Statement 2 is incorrect: it was the Bangkok Conference of June 1942 that placed the INA under the Indian Independence League. Statement 4 is incorrect: the Japanese wanted only a token force of about 2,000 men.

st.3: Officials were socially boycotted at Duggirala.
st.1: Pullari was a tax on cutting timber in forest lands.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: pullari was a tax on grazing cattle in forest lands. Statement 3 is incorrect: the social boycott of officials was at Macherla in Palnadu, not Duggirala. Statement 4 is incorrect: the movement began in 1921.

st.1: Lala Har Dayal
st.2: V.D. Savarkar

st.3: The 1973 Act fixed a standard holding of 10–27 acres of dry land or 35–54 acres of wet land.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the bill was brought under P.V. Narasimha Rao, not Kasu Brahmananda Reddy. Statement 3 is incorrect: the standard holding was 10–27 acres of wet land or 35–54 acres of dry land, not the reverse.

st.3: The Matsya Purana is a main source of Satavahana genealogy.

x: All three statements are correct. The Matsya Purana, a main source of Satavahana genealogy, dates their rule to 271 BC - 174 AD, while the Vayu and Vishnu Puranas mention 17 kings and 272 years.

st.3: Upasika Bodhisri made her gifts at Nagarjunakonda in the reign of Virapurushadatta.

x: All three statements are correct. Santamula overthrew Pulomavi III c. AD 225-230, Pulomavi III ended his days at Myakadoni, and Bodhisri's gifts at Nagarjunakonda fall in the reign of Virapurushadatta.

st.3: Its original Paishachi text is lost and survives only through later Sanskrit versions.

x: All three statements are correct. The Brihatkatha had 7 lakh verses in 7 stories and mentions slavery; its Paishachi original is lost and is known only through later Sanskrit versions such as the Kathasaritsagara.

st.1: They were the first rulers to make tax-free land grants, but only to Brahmanas.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the Satavahanas made tax-free land grants to Buddhists as well as Brahmanas. Statement 2 is incorrect: gold coins were first issued in India by the Indo-Greeks/Kushanas, not the Satavahanas.

st.4: Telugu words such as atta, potta and pilla occur in it, though it is written in Sanskrit.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: it contains about 700 gathas. Statement 4 is incorrect: it is written in Maharashtri Prakrit, not Sanskrit, though Telugu words occur in it.

st.4: Its influence was confined to the Deccan and did not reach Sri Lanka.
st.1: James Burgess called it the 'epitome of Indian architecture' and wrote 'Tree and Serpent Worship'.
st.3: A large part of its sculptures is in the Louvre in Paris.

x: None of the statements is correct. It was James Fergusson, not Burgess, who called Amaravati the 'epitome of Indian architecture' and wrote 'Tree and Serpent Worship'. The oldest stupa in AP is at Bhattiprolu. A large part of the sculptures is in the British Museum (and Chennai), not the Louvre. Its influence reached Sri Lanka (Anuradhapura) and South-East Asia.

st.4: They were the immediate predecessors of the Satavahanas in the Krishna valley.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: inscriptions confirm only some of the kings named in the Puranas. Statement 4 is incorrect: the Ikshvakus were the immediate successors, not predecessors, of the Satavahanas in the Krishna valley.

st.1: Upasika Bodhisri, daughter of Revanta of Amaravati, was a royal donor ranked first among women donors.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: Bodhisri was a non-royal donor, which is why her record is evidence of non-royal patronage. Statement 2 is incorrect: most of the records are in Prakrit. Statement 3 is correct: the Ikshvakus were the first to date records by year, month and day.

st.3: Gunaga Vijayaditya issued the Maliyapundi grant for a Jain temple at Dharmapuri.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the Kaluchumbarru grant was won by the courtesan Chamekamba. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Maliyapundi grant was issued by Ammaraja II, not Gunaga Vijayaditya.

st.3: As Jananathapura, Draksharama was the coronation seat of the Reddi kings of Kondavidu.
st.1: The Skanda Purana and Potana's Bhimeswara Puranam are literary sources on the Draksharama temple.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the Bhimeswara Puranam is by Srinatha, not Potana. Statement 2 is incorrect: Draksharama, not Samalkot, is the Trilinga kshetra. Statement 3 is incorrect: Jananathapura (Draksharama) was the coronation seat of the Chalukya-Chola viceroys of Vengi, not the Reddis.

st.2: After 1323 Andhra was placed under Zafar Khan.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the Vilasa grant says the captured Prataparudra died on the banks of the Narmada. Statement 2 is incorrect: after 1323 Andhra was placed under Malik Burhanuddin; Zafar Khan founded the Bahmani kingdom later (1347).

st.2: Each Nayaka held a fort and kept troops but paid no tribute.
st.1: The kingdom was divided into 72 Nayankaras held by military officers (Nayakas).

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: there were 77 Nayankaras, not 72. Statement 2 is incorrect: each Nayaka paid a fixed tribute to the king. Statement 3 is incorrect: about three-fourths of the land was under Nayankara, not one-half.

st.2: The Ayagars were paid by a share of the village produce and by rent-free land.

x: All three statements are correct. The twelve Ayagars were paid by a share of the produce and rent-free land, not cash salaries; the Talari was the watchman and the Karanam the accountant.

st.1: Under the truce of 1364-65 he ceded Warangal and paid 33 lakhs and a turquoise throne.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: under the truce he ceded Golconda, not Warangal. Statement 4 is incorrect: he was killed at Bhimavaram by Anapota Nayaka of the Recherla family, not by Anapota Reddi.

st.3: It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site on 25 July 2019.
st.2: Its deity is Shiva as Ramalingeswara, and it is named after Lord Rama.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the temple is named after its sculptor Ramappa. Statement 3 is incorrect: it was inscribed on 25 July 2021. Statement 4 is incorrect: Palampet is in Mulugu district.

st.1: It submitted its report on 7 February 1953.

x: All three statements are correct. Appointed in December 1952 after Nehru's statement of 19 December 1952, the single-member Wanchoo Committee reported on 7 February 1953; the Centre's decisions followed on 25 March 1953.

st.1: C.P. Brown's English-Telugu dictionary

st.4: He became General Secretary of the All India Public Library Association at its first conference in Madras in 1919.
st.2: Kandukuri Veeresalingam, not he, said, 'Library Movement in Andhra is Swayambhu'.

Statement 2 is incorrect: it was Ayyanki himself who said the movement is 'Swayambhu'. Statement 4 is incorrect: he became General Secretary at the second conference, in December 1923.

st.1: Gurram Jashuva's 1919 Machilipatnam Adi-Andhra conference demanded abolition of the Jogini and Devadasi systems.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the 1919 Machilipatnam Adi-Andhra conference was Bhagya Reddy Varma's. Statement 3 is incorrect: arrack was prohibited from 1 October 1993.

st.4: Kandiseekudu means 'The Bat'.
st.3: Gabbilam is modelled on Kalidasa's Kumarasambhava.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the bat carries the message to Lord Shiva (Kashi Vishweswara), not Vishnu. Statement 3 is incorrect: Gabbilam is modelled on the Meghaduta. Statement 4 is incorrect: Kandiseekudu means 'The Refugee'; Gabbilam means 'The Bat'.

st.2: The Dadasaheb Phalke Award was started in 1959.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the Nandi Awards are given by the Andhra Pradesh Government, not the Centre. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Dadasaheb Phalke Award was started in 1969.

st.2: The Drafting Committee, set up on 29 August 1947, was chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.

x: All three statements are correct. Sachchidananda Sinha was temporary President, the Drafting Committee of 29 August 1947 was chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, and B.N. Rau later sat on the International Court of Justice.

st.2: Vatsa lay on the Yamuna with its capital at Mathura.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: Vatsa's capital was Kaushambi; Mathura was the capital of Surasena. Statement 3 is incorrect: Ujjayini was Avanti's northern capital; the southern capital was Mahishmati.

st.1: Heliodorus came as the envoy of Menander to the Shunga king Bhagabhadra.
st.4: The Smritis call the Greeks absorbed into Indian society degenerate Shudras.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: Heliodorus was the envoy of Antialcidas, not Menander. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Besnagar pillar honours Vasudeva, not Sankarshana. Statement 4 is incorrect: the Smritis call them Vratya (degenerate) Kshatriyas, not Shudras.

st.4: Talaq-e-Hasan is talaq pronounced three times at one sitting.
st.1: A Muslim marriage (Nikah) is solemnised by a Kazi, under the Kazis Act, 1937.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the Kazis Act dates from 1880; 1937 is the Shariat Application Act. Statement 3 is incorrect: Khula is divorce at the wife's instance. Statement 4 is incorrect: Talaq-e-Hasan is pronounced once a month over three months; three at one sitting is Talaq-e-Biddat.

st.2: Abbé Dubois saw caste as a product of race.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: Risley ranked castes by social precedence in the 1901 Census. Statement 2 is incorrect: Abbé Dubois saw caste as a Brahmin device for purity; the racial theory is Risley's.

st.3: Robert Redfield's 'The Little Community' was published in 1956.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: homogeneity, not cultural diversity, is an element of a rural community. Statement 3 is incorrect: 'The Little Community' was published in 1955; 'Peasant Society and Culture' came in 1956.

st.1: PM-JANMAN was launched on 15 November 2023 (Janjatiya Gaurav Divas) and covers all 75 PVTGs and all other Scheduled Tribes.
st.4: The total outlay of PM-JANMAN is ₹34,104 crore.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: PM-JANMAN covers the 75 PVTGs only, not all Scheduled Tribes. Statement 2 is incorrect: the first PVTG with habitat rights was the Bharia of Madhya Pradesh. Statement 4 is incorrect: the outlay is ₹24,104 crore.

st.1: The original Article 338 provided for a National Commission for SCs and STs.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the original Article 338 provided for a Special Officer (Commissioner for SCs and STs). Statement 2 is incorrect: the joint Commission became constitutional in 1990; the 1978 Commission was non-statutory.

st.2: The term 'Harijan' was coined by Gandhi.

st.2: Gig workers form about 2% of India's workforce.

st.1: It was restructured from the Rajiv Awas Yojana.

st.2: All four Labour Codes came into force on 21 November 2024.

st.3: In the Kulbhushan Jadhav case, the ICJ ruled in India's favour.

st.3: The Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative has five pillars.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Shangri-La Dialogue is organised by the International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS). Statement 3 is incorrect: the IPOI has seven pillars.

st.1: The UN Charter was signed by 50 nations at San Francisco on 24 October 1945.
st.2: Ukraine, which signed later, became the 51st original member.

st.3: Citizenship by descent applies to a person born outside India only if the father was an Indian citizen at the time of birth.

st.3: It held that the floor of the House, not the Governor's opinion, is the test of a ministry's majority.

st.3: Article 17 (abolition of untouchability) falls under the Right to Equality.
