st.1: It was decided by a nine-judge bench by a 5:4 majority.
st.4: It ordered a permanent body for backward classes, which led to the Mandal Commission.
st.2: It upheld 27% reservation for OBCs, including the creamy layer.

x: None of the statements is correct. The nine-judge bench decided by 6:3, not 5:4. It upheld 27% OBC reservation with the creamy layer excluded. It did not permit reservation in promotions. The permanent body it ordered became the NCBC; the Mandal Commission had reported earlier (1980).

st.2: The National Security Act was enacted in 1971 and allows detention up to 12 months without charges.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: in January 2026 the Supreme Court held that delay alone is not a trump card for bail in UAPA cases. Statement 2 is incorrect: the NSA was enacted in 1980; 1971 was MISA.

st.2: The combined share of the BC-A to BC-E groups is 25 per cent.
st.1: The BC-E group has a 7 per cent quota.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: BC-E has a 4 per cent quota. Statement 2 is incorrect: the combined BC-A to BC-E share is 29 per cent; 25 per cent was the earlier A-D quota. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Anantharaman Commission reported in 1970.

st.1: In Ranganatha Reddy (1977), Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer's majority view held that it includes all privately owned resources.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: Krishna Iyer's view in Ranganatha Reddy was a minority view. Statement 3 is incorrect: the 2024 judgment held that not every privately owned resource is a 'material resource of the community'.

st.2: Article 371D provides for a Central University in Andhra Pradesh.
st.4: Section 97 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 amended Article 371E to cover Telangana.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Central University is under Article 371E, not 371D. Statement 3 is incorrect: bifurcation under Articles 3 and 4 needs no constitutional amendment. Statement 4 is incorrect: Section 97 amended Article 371D, not 371E.

st.2: Its appointed day was 1 March 2014.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the appointed day was 2 June 2014. Statement 3 is incorrect: companies and corporations are in the Ninth Schedule; the Tenth Schedule lists institutions.

st.2: It was set up in 2007 and reported in 2012.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Punchhi Commission was set up in 2007 and reported in 2010. Statement 3 is incorrect: appointment by a committee including the Lok Sabha Speaker was the NCRWC's recommendation, not Punchhi's.

st.3: Surya Kant, the 53rd CJI, succeeded B.R. Gavai.

x: All three statements are correct. N.V. Ramana (48th CJI) was from Andhra Pradesh, D.Y. Chandrachud was the 50th CJI, and Surya Kant, the 53rd, succeeded B.R. Gavai.

st.1: A removal motion must be signed by at least 50 Lok Sabha or 100 Rajya Sabha members.
st.4: Soumitra Sen was removed in 2011 after both Houses passed the motion.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the motion needs 100 Lok Sabha or 50 Rajya Sabha members. Statement 3 is incorrect: the motion against V. Ramaswami failed in the Lok Sabha. Statement 4 is incorrect: Soumitra Sen resigned before the Lok Sabha voted.

st.3: Tamil Nadu has India's first fully paperless district court.
st.1: The first Lok Adalat camp was held in Maharashtra in 1982.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the first Lok Adalat camp was held in Gujarat. Statement 3 is incorrect: the first fully paperless district court is in Kerala. Statement 4 is incorrect: the North-Eastern and Himalayan States share 90:10, not 80:20.

st.4: During a Financial Emergency, State Money Bills cannot be reserved for the President.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the extension can continue only up to six months after the Emergency ends. Statement 4 is incorrect: during a Financial Emergency State Money Bills may be reserved for the President.

st.4: The 101st Amendment inserted Articles 246A, 268A and 279A.
st.2: GST came into force on 1 April 2017.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: GST came into force on 1 July 2017. Statement 3 is incorrect: GST is destination-based. Statement 4 is incorrect: the Amendment inserted Article 269A; Article 268A was omitted.

st.1: The Chief Electoral Officer is provided for under Section 13A of the RPA 1950 and is a constitutional authority.
st.3: The Chief Electoral Officer is appointed by the State Government in consultation with the ECI.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the CEO is a statutory, not constitutional, authority. Statement 2 is incorrect: the State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor. Statement 3 is incorrect: the CEO is appointed by the ECI in consultation with the State Government.

st.1: The theme of Human Rights Day 2024 was 'Our Rights, Our Future, Right Now'.

x: All three statements are correct. 'Our Rights, Our Future, Right Now' was the 2024 theme, 'Human Rights, Our Everyday Essentials' the 2025 theme, and 20 November marks the adoption of the UNCRC in 1989.

st.1: NITI Aayog first released the Business Reform Action Plan (BRAP) ranking of States in 2015.
st.4: Post-1991 delicensing reduced competition among States for private and foreign investment.
st.3: According to the convergence view, richer and industrialised States attracted most post-1991 private investment, widening regional gaps.

x: None of the statements is correct. BRAP rankings are released by DPIIT, not NITI Aayog. In BRAP 2019 Andhra Pradesh ranked first, followed by Uttar Pradesh and Telangana. Widening gaps from investment going to richer States is the divergence view, not the convergence view. Delicensing made States compete harder for investment.

st.1: The Narasimha Rao government's panchayat bills of September 1991 were scrutinised by a Select Committee of the Lok Sabha.
st.4: National Panchayati Raj Day is observed on 2 October.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the bills were scrutinised by a Joint Parliamentary Committee. Statement 3 is incorrect: the 73rd Amendment came into force on 24 April 1993. Statement 4 is incorrect: National Panchayati Raj Day is 24 April.

st.2: The extent of High Court jurisdiction over the village courts of the tribal areas is specified by the Governor.

x: All three statements are correct. A District Council has 30 members (26 elected, 4 nominated by the Governor), the Governor specifies the High Court's jurisdiction over village courts, and Section 10(26) exempts certain incomes of STs in these areas.

st.2: Reservation of Chairperson posts for women arose from the 73rd Amendment rather than from a long-standing rural demand.

x: All three statements are correct. The NCW was set up in 1992 under the 1990 Act, reservation of chairperson posts for women came from the 73rd Amendment, and the Chattopadhyay-Duflo study found women leaders invested more in water and roads.

st.3: A special sports school for tribal children was set up at Araku Valley in Andhra Pradesh in 2022.
st.2: The Dr Ambedkar Centres of Excellence give free Civil Services coaching to OBC students in Central Universities.

x: None of the statements is correct. SHRESHTA gives seats to meritorious SC students in private residential schools. The Ambedkar Centres of Excellence coach SC, not OBC, students. The Araku Valley sports school for tribal children was set up in 2016.

st.2: Its full-time members hold the rank of Cabinet Minister.
st.4: It is the nodal agency for estimating GDP in India.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: full-time members have Minister of State rank. Statement 3 is incorrect: Arvind Panagariya was the first Vice-Chairman. Statement 4 is incorrect: GDP is estimated by MoSPI's National Statistics Office; NITI Aayog is the nodal body for poverty estimation.

st.2: Sagarmala (2015), the port-led development programme, is implemented by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.

x: All three statements are correct. Bharatmala is implemented through NHAI/MoRTH, Sagarmala by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, and the NIP envisaged ₹111 lakh crore for 2020-25.

st.2: Hood's doctrines stress output controls rather than input controls.

x: All three statements are correct. Christopher Hood popularised NPM in 1991; it stresses output controls over input controls and features performance auditing and contracting out.

st.3: AP's rail network is 100% electrified.

x: All three statements are correct. The Errupalem-Amaravati-Namburu line was approved in October 2024, Ramayapatnam-Kadapa is a steel plant line, and AP's rail network is 100% electrified.

st.2: As per SRS 2024, India's Under-5 Mortality Rate is 24.
st.4: As per SRS 2016-20, India's life expectancy at birth is 72.5 years.
st.1: As per SRS 2024, India's Infant Mortality Rate is 28 per 1,000 live births.

x: None of the statements is correct. The IMR is 24 and the U5MR 28 (the figures are swapped). MMR is measured per 1,00,000 live births, not per 1,000. Life expectancy at birth for 2016-20 is 70.0 years.

st.3: Vijayawada was the largest urban agglomeration.
st.2: Krishna was the most urbanised district, followed by Visakhapatnam.

x: None of the statements is correct. AP's urban share of 29.5% was below the all-India 31.2%. Visakhapatnam, not Krishna, was the most urbanised district. Visakhapatnam, not Vijayawada, was the largest urban agglomeration.

st.1: MGNREGA, 2005 was India's first rights-based welfare legislation, covering urban as well as rural households.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: MGNREGA covers rural households only. Statement 2 is incorrect: the IRDP pilot began in 1978.

st.1: It guarantees 100 days of wage work.
st.3: Its cost is borne fully by the Centre.
st.4: Its national launch was held at Bandlapalli in Anantapur district.

x: None of the statements is correct. It guarantees 125 days of work, not 100. Work can be paused for up to 60 days in the peak season, not 90. The cost is shared 60:40 between the Centre and States. The national launch was at Mukkavaripalli in Tirupati district; Bandlapalli was MGNREGA's launch site (2006).

st.2: It kept devolution at 41 percent.

x: All three statements are correct. The 16th Finance Commission added a contribution criterion (square root of GSDP), retained the income-distance criterion and kept vertical devolution at 41 percent.

st.1: As per the India Employment Report 2024, the share of regular wage/salaried employment (22.7%) was higher than that of casual employment (21.5%) in 2022.
st.3: As per Q2 FY26 data, about 65.2 crore persons aged 15 and above were employed.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: casual employment (22.7%) was higher than regular wage employment (21.5%). Statement 3 is incorrect: about 56.2 crore persons were employed. Statement 4 is incorrect: regular salaried jobs are about 49.8% of urban jobs.

st.2: Monthly per capita consumption expenditure is an economic indicator of poverty.

x: All three statements are correct. Lack of safe drinking water is a social indicator, MPCE is an economic indicator, and the MPI covers health, education and living standards.

st.3: Programmes such as SFDA, DPAP, ITDP and IADP were run through parallel agencies that bypassed the panchayats.

x: All three statements are correct. Economic and social planning is in the Concurrent List, Article 40 directs the organisation of village panchayats, and target-group programmes such as SFDA, DPAP, ITDP and IADP bypassed the panchayats.

st.2: It was broadly modelled on the US Tennessee Valley Authority.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Planning Commission was broadly modelled on the Soviet Gosplan; the TVA was the model for the DVC. Statement 3 is incorrect: it was set up by a Cabinet resolution of March 1950, not on the National Planning Committee's recommendation.

st.3: General Category States such as Andhra Pradesh received assistance in a grant : loan ratio of 30 : 70.

x: All three statements are correct. Under Gadgil-Mukherjee, population had 60%, per capita income 25% and fiscal performance 7.5% weight, and General Category States got a 30 : 70 grant-loan mix (Special Category 90 : 10).

st.2: Rolling Plan of the Janata Government
st.4: Launch of the Fourth Five Year Plan

x: The Plan Holiday (1966-69) came first, followed by the launch of the Fourth Plan (1969), the Janata Government's Rolling Plan (1978-80), and the Annual Plans before the Eighth Plan (1990-92).

st.1: The Aspirational Districts Programme was launched in January 2018 and covers 250 districts.
st.4: Agriculture and Education carry 30% weight each in the district ranking.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the programme covers 112 districts. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Aspirational Blocks Programme tracks 500 blocks on 40 KPIs, not 60. Statement 4 is incorrect: Health and Nutrition and Education carry 30% each; Agriculture carries 20%.

st.2: India was 112th in the Sustainable Development Report 2024.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: India was 109th in the SDR 2024 (112th was in 2023). Statement 3 is incorrect: NITI Aayog, not MoSPI, is India's nodal body for the GII.

st.2: The excess reserve ratio is the fixed percentage of deposits that every bank must keep as reserves.
st.1: If a ₹10 note changes hands twice in a period, it supports ₹20 of transactions – this is the idea of the money multiplier.
st.4: The Digital Rupee was made legal tender by amending the Banking Regulation Act through the Finance Act, 2022.

x: None of the statements is correct. A note changing hands several times illustrates the velocity of money, not the multiplier. The fixed share banks must keep is the required reserve ratio, not the excess reserve ratio. An expansion of currency lowers the value of money. The Digital Rupee was made legal tender by amending the RBI Act.

st.1: The money multiplier in India was 4.21 on 31 December 2025.
st.3: About 74 billion banknotes were in circulation in May 2026.
st.2: The CRR was raised by 100 basis points to 5.0% of NDTL, absorbing about ₹2.5 lakh crore.

x: None of the statements is correct. The money multiplier was 6.21. The CRR was cut, not raised, by 100 basis points to 3.0%, releasing about ₹2.5 lakh crore. About 174 billion notes were in circulation in May 2026. M3 (12.1%) grew faster than M0 (2.9%).

st.1: The minimum Net Owned Fund for a housing finance company is ₹10 crore.
st.4: The NBFC Ombudsman Scheme, 2018 was merged into the Banking Ombudsman Scheme, 2006.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: an HFC needs a minimum NOF of ₹20 crore. Statement 3 is incorrect: the 2026-27 Upper Layer list has 17 companies and Tata Sons was not allowed to surrender its licence. Statement 4 is incorrect: the 2018 scheme was merged into the RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021.

st.2: 122nd Amendment Bill is tabled
st.1: 101st Amendment Act gets Presidential assent

x: The 122nd Amendment Bill was tabled first (2014), then the 101st Amendment Act received Presidential assent (September 2016), GST was rolled out (1 July 2017), and GST 2.0 came into effect (2025).

st.1: Marine products are not among AP's top exports.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: marine products are among AP's top exports. Statement 2 is incorrect: Visakhapatnam Port's share of India's marine exports did not fall in 2024-25.

st.3: John Stuart Mill propounded the theory of comparative advantage.
st.4: The 'direction' of trade refers to its commodity-wise pattern.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: export promotion is outward-looking and import substitution inward-looking. Statement 3 is incorrect: comparative advantage was propounded by David Ricardo, not J.S. Mill. Statement 4 is incorrect: 'direction' is the country-wise pattern; the commodity-wise pattern is 'composition'.

st.2: Strong services exports have partly offset the merchandise trade deficit since 1991.

x: All three statements are correct. The deficit peaked at US$195.66 bn in 2012-13, a services surplus has partly offset the merchandise deficit since 1991, and merchandise exports were US$437.7 bn in 2024-25.

st.1: India exports iron ore to China as a major item.

x: All three statements are correct. Iron ore is a major export to China (India does not import it from China), labour-intensive exports shifted away from the US in April-November 2025, and QCOs, NTBs and PLI respond to dependence on China.

st.4: The overall BoP surplus of $20.8 billion in July 2026 was driven by the Government's sovereign green bond issue.
st.1: India's forex reserves first crossed US$ 100 billion in December 2005.
st.3: Reserves of $682.3 billion on 29 May 2026 gave about 6 months of import cover.

x: None of the statements is correct. Reserves first crossed US$100 billion in December 2003. In January 1991 they had fallen to about US$1.2 billion, not 12 billion. $682.3 billion gave about 11 months of import cover. The July 2026 surplus was driven by the RBI's special FCNR(B) deposit scheme.

st.3: Andhra Pradesh has 22 soil categories, of which 10 cover over 88% of the State.

x: All three statements are correct. The Planning Commission (1989) drew 15 agro-climatic regions; coastal AP is in the East Coast Plains and Hills and Rayalaseema in the Southern Plateau and Hills; AP has 22 soil categories, 10 of which cover over 88% of the State.

st.1: Rabi crops depend mainly on the south-west monsoon rains and on irrigation.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: rabi crops depend on winter rain from western disturbances, not the south-west monsoon. Statement 3 is incorrect: kharif crops are sown in June-July.

st.1: According to the World Food Conference 1974, food security exists when all people, at all times, have physical and economic access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: this definition is from the World Food Summit 1996; the 1974 Conference stressed food supply. Statement 2 is incorrect: Sen's entitlement approach was set out in 'Poverty and Famines' (1981).

st.1: It was announced in the Union Budget 2017-18 for tomato, onion and potato.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: Operation Greens was announced in the Union Budget 2018-19. Statement 2 is incorrect: it is implemented by the Ministry of Food Processing Industries.

st.3: The food subsidy allocation in the Union Budget 2026-27 is Rs 2,72,629 crore.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: NSSF borrowing ended and food subsidy came on budget in 2021-22. Statement 3 is incorrect: the 2026-27 allocation is Rs 2,27,629 crore.

st.2: It is the maximum price that may be charged, meant to protect producers.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: a guaranteed minimum price is a floor price (such as MSP). Statement 2 is incorrect: a ceiling price is a maximum price meant to protect consumers, not producers.

st.4: It gave no importance to technological upgradation and modernisation.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: it built on the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956. Statement 4 is incorrect: it emphasised technological upgradation and modernisation.

st.3: It has been called the 'Bible of Liberalisation'.
st.1: It was placed before Parliament by T.T. Krishnamachari on 30 April 1956.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: it was placed before Parliament by Jawaharlal Nehru. Statement 2 is incorrect: the 'socialistic pattern' goal was adopted at the Avadi session (1955). Statement 3 is incorrect: it was called the 'Bible of State Capitalism'.

st.4: After 79 more items were dereserved in February 2008, 21 items remained reserved.
st.1: Reservation began in 1977 with 47 items.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: reservation began in 1967. Statement 2 is incorrect: the last 20 items were dereserved in 2015. Statement 4 is incorrect: after February 2008, 35 items remained reserved.

st.1: CGTMSE began as the Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme for Small Industries, launched on 30 August 2000 by the Government of India and NABARD.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the scheme was launched by the Government of India and SIDBI, not NABARD. Statement 3 is incorrect: MUDRA is a wholly owned subsidiary of SIDBI.

st.2: In 2023-24 Kerala and Tamil Nadu topped the Index with a score of 79.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: in 2020-21 AP shared 4th place and did not retain 2nd rank. Statement 2 is incorrect: Kerala and Uttarakhand, not Tamil Nadu, topped the 2023-24 Index with 79.

st.2: In 2023-24 the shares of AP and Telangana in national GDP were 4.9% and 4.7% respectively.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: metro Hyderabad produces about 47.5% of Telangana's output. Statement 2 is incorrect: AP's share was 4.7% and Telangana's 4.9%, not the reverse.

st.1: The slowest growth, 4.10%, was in 2020-21.
st.2: The fastest growth, 15.26%, was in 2022-23.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the slowest growth, 4.10%, was in 2019-20. Statement 2 is incorrect: the fastest growth, 15.26%, was in 2021-22.

st.3: The Industrial Development Policy 4.0 covers 2023-28.
st.1: Sri City, a bulk-drug SEZ, is in Tirupati district.
st.4: Twelve BHAVYA industrial parks were proposed in August 2026.

x: None of the statements is correct. Sri City is a multi-product SEZ, not a bulk-drug SEZ. Royal Enfield's unit is in the Rayalaseema hub near Tirupati, not the Visakhapatnam bulk-drug cluster. The Industrial Development Policy 4.0 covers 2024-29. Six, not twelve, BHAVYA parks were proposed.

st.1: It is shared 90:10 (Centre:State) for general States.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the general-State share is 75:25, not 90:10. Statement 2 is incorrect: North-Eastern/Himalayan States share 90:10.

st.3: The Centre funds 100% of the remaining cost of the irrigation component of Polavaram.

x: All three statements are correct. The measure was approved on 15 March 2017, the Centre repays EAP loans (2015-16 to 2019-20) bearing 90% of the cost, and it funds 100% of the remaining irrigation cost of Polavaram.

st.2: The Centre repays the loan and interest up to the SCS-equivalent 90% share.

x: All three statements are correct. AP borrows from the World Bank, ADB and others, and for EAPs signed and disbursed in 2015-16 to 2019-20 the Centre repays loan and interest up to the SCS-equivalent 90% share.

st.4: The Veterinary Biological Research Institute is at Tirupati.
st.2: Pashu KCC gives collateral-free credit up to Rs 1.60 lakh only to landowning farmers.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: Pashu KCC's collateral-free credit up to Rs 1.60 lakh is not limited to landowning farmers. Statement 3 is incorrect: prompt repayers pay an effective 4% interest. Statement 4 is incorrect: the VBRI is at Vijayawada.

st.1: It targets an investment of Rs 1 lakh crore.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the policy targets an investment of Rs 50,000 crore. Statement 2 is incorrect: the 175+ MSME parks are one per Assembly constituency, not per district.

st.2: India ranked 39th in the Global Innovation Index 2025.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: India ranked 38th in GII 2025 (39th was 2024). Statement 3 is incorrect: Switzerland ranked first.

st.1: NHP 2017 targets public health spending of 3% of GDP by 2025.
st.2: The 176th Report of the Public Accounts Committee puts government health expenditure at 1.43% of GDP.
st.3: Household out-of-pocket expenditure was 53.4% of total health expenditure in 2022-23.

x: None of the statements is correct. NHP 2017 targets 2.5% of GDP, not 3%. The 176th Report is of the Standing Committee on Health, not the PAC. Out-of-pocket expenditure was 43.4%, not 53.4%. The 'missing middle' is about 40 crore people, not 10 crore.

st.1: The NSE was set up in November 1992 on the recommendation of the Narasimham Committee.
st.2: The NSE was recognised by SEBI in April 1994.
st.4: BSE brokers moved to Nariman Point, Mumbai in 1874.

x: None of the statements is correct. The NSE was set up on the recommendation of the Pherwani Committee. It was recognised by SEBI in April 1993. Its first segment was the Wholesale Debt Market (June 1994), not the Cash Market. BSE brokers moved to Dalal Street in 1874.

st.3: Fifteen REITs were listed in India in 2026.
st.2: Foreign Portfolio Investors register through the SWAGAT-FI single window launched in 2022.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the FPI single window was launched in 2025. Statement 3 is incorrect: five REITs were listed in 2026. Statement 4 is incorrect: CRISIL (1987) was India's first credit rating agency; ICRA came in 1991.

st.4: From 23 September to 21 December, days in the Northern Hemisphere become progressively longer.
st.2: The North Pole is lit from 23 September to 21 March, about six months.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the North Pole is lit from 21 March to 23 September. Statement 3 is incorrect: when one pole has continuous daylight the other has continuous night. Statement 4 is incorrect: from 23 September to 21 December northern days become shorter.

st.3: In summer the Sun's altitude is higher and noon shadows are shorter.

x: All three statements are correct. The summer hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun, oblique rays spread energy over a larger area, and in summer the higher Sun casts shorter noon shadows.

st.1: The Peninsula remained joined to Africa until the Eocene.
st.2: The Deccan Traps erupted as India passed over the Kerguelen hotspot near the equator.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the Peninsula separated from Africa by the Cretaceous; the Eocene is when the collision with Eurasia began. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Deccan Traps are linked to the Réunion hotspot; Kerguelen is linked to the Rajmahal Traps. Statement 4 is incorrect: India moves about 5 cm a year and the Himalayas rise about 5 mm a year.

st.1: Magnitude above about 6.5, a deep focus and vertical sea-floor movement favour a tsunami.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: a shallow, not deep, focus favours a tsunami. Statement 3 is incorrect: ITEWC at INCOIS is in Hyderabad, not Chennai.

st.1: Andhra Pradesh lies in Zones III and IV.
st.2: Vijayawada lies in Zone II and Visakhapatnam in Zone III.
st.4: New Delhi lies in Zone V.

x: None of the statements is correct. Andhra Pradesh lies in Zones II and III, with no area in Zone IV or V. Vijayawada is in Zone III and Visakhapatnam in Zone II. Hyderabad lies in Zone II. New Delhi lies in Zone IV.

st.1: Mountains are formed only by folding.
st.4: Valleys are formed only by river erosion.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: mountains also form by faulting, volcanism and erosion. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Aravallis and Urals are old fold mountains. Statement 4 is incorrect: valleys are also formed by glaciers, tectonics and karst processes.

st.1: The Southern Ocean is the smallest ocean.
st.4: Oceans cover about 60–61% of the Earth's surface.
st.3: The Atlantic has the most islands, about 25,000.

x: None of the statements is correct. The Arctic is the smallest ocean. The Atlantic is the second largest; the Indian Ocean is third. The Pacific, not the Atlantic, has the most islands. Oceans cover about 70–71% of the Earth's surface.

st.3: Puerto Rico, a US territory, is less densely populated than Mexico, Brazil or Argentina.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the Galapagos belong to Ecuador, not Peru. Statement 3 is incorrect: Puerto Rico is more densely populated than Mexico, Brazil or Argentina.

st.2: Compared with a hurricane, a tornado is larger, land-based and lasts only minutes.
st.1: Tornado winds range from about 30 to 60 km/h.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: tornado winds range from about 105 to 322 km/h. Statement 2 is incorrect: a tornado is much smaller than a hurricane. Statement 4 is incorrect: tornadoes are usually spawned by supercell thunderstorms.

st.4: During Cyclone Montha, the IMD system AWARE 2.0 auto-triggered evacuations and alerts.
st.1: Cyclones such as Hudhud, Titli, Michaung and Montha hit the State mostly in April–June.
st.2: The State has a coastline of about 1,553 km.

x: None of the statements is correct. These cyclones struck mostly in October–December. AP's coastline is about 1,053 km. Montha made landfall near Kakinada, not Visakhapatnam. AWARE 2.0 is the State's RTGS system, not an IMD system.

st.2: The Campos are tropical grasslands of Argentina.
st.1: The Llanos of the Amazon basin are tropical grasslands.
st.3: The United Nations has declared 2027 the International Year for Rangelands and Pastoralists.

x: None of the statements is correct. The Llanos lie in the Orinoco basin, not the Amazon. The Campos are in Brazil, not Argentina. The UN International Year for Rangelands and Pastoralists is 2026. The Downs are temperate, not tropical, grasslands.

st.1: Daman and Diu remained under Portuguese rule until 1961.

x: All three statements are correct. Daman and Diu were freed from Portuguese rule in 1961, India has nine coastal States, and Puducherry is a coastal Union Territory.

st.2: Nanda Devi and Trisul belong to the Greater Himalaya (Himadri).

x: All three statements are correct. Nanda Devi is the highest peak wholly within India, it and Trisul belong to the Greater Himalaya, and it lies in the Kumaon Himalaya of Uttarakhand.

st.2: Kingri-Wingri and Muling La are passes of Uttarakhand.

x: All three statements are correct. Mana pass north of Badrinath leads to Tibet, Kingri-Wingri and Muling La are Uttarakhand passes, and Lipulekh lies at the India–China–Nepal tri-junction.

st.3: Tunnel erosion is the removal of soil by wind.
st.2: Rill erosion is the final stage of water erosion.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: gully erosion, not rill erosion, is the final stage. Statement 3 is incorrect: tunnel erosion is subsurface removal of soil by water. Statement 4 is incorrect: running water is the most powerful agent of soil erosion.

st.1: 'Edaphic' refers to the climatic factor of the environment.
st.4: The saline soils of the Rayalaseema plateau, high in lime and salt, are highly fertile for cropping.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: 'edaphic' refers to the soil factor. Statement 3 is incorrect: arid soil has low moisture retention. Statement 4 is incorrect: these saline soils are unfit for cropping.

st.3: The Makran subduction zone is a tsunami source for India's east coast.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: Odisha falls in the high tsunami-risk zone. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Makran zone threatens the west coast, not the east coast.

st.1: Operation Phuktal (2015) blasted a landslide-debris lake on the Phuktal river in Spiti, Himachal Pradesh.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the Phuktal river lake was in Zanskar, Kargil, not Spiti. Statement 2 is incorrect: a GLOF typically comes from a moraine-dammed proglacial lake, not a supraglacial lake on the glacier.

st.1: India receives about 1,869 bcm of water from rainfall a year.
st.3: Per-capita water availability has risen from about 1,400 m³ at Independence to over 5,000 m³.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: India receives about 3,880 bcm from rainfall; 1,869 bcm is the average annual water resource. Statement 3 is incorrect: per-capita availability has fallen from over 5,000 m³ to about 1,400 m³. Statement 4 is incorrect: agriculture, not industry, is the largest user.

st.1: It is degraded land that cannot be brought under vegetative cover even with great effort.
st.2: It is mapped only through ground-based village surveys.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: wasteland can be brought under vegetative cover with reasonable effort. Statement 2 is incorrect: it is mapped through satellite-based National Wastelands Monitoring.

st.2: The Cuddapah basin spreads mainly over the Kadapa, Kurnool, Prakasam and Guntur districts.

x: All three statements are correct. The Proterozoic Cuddapah basin (about 1.6 billion years old) lies mainly in Kadapa, Kurnool, Prakasam and Guntur and holds barytes, asbestos, steatite, limestone, uranium and diamonds.

st.3: The Ravva oil and gas field was discovered by ONGC in 1987.

x: All three statements are correct. India aims at a 15% gas share by 2030, JHBDPL is the Urja Ganga pipeline, and the Ravva field was discovered by ONGC in 1987 (Cairn later operated it).

st.4: Jute-ICARE stands for Integrated Crop and Advanced Research Exercise.
st.1: The Jute Packaging Materials Act, 1987 requires 20% of food grains and 100% of sugar to be packed in jute.
st.3: The Cotton Corporation of India buys raw jute at the MSP when market prices fall.

x: None of the statements is correct. The Act requires 100% of food grains and 20% of sugar in jute, not the reverse. Paat-Mitro is for jute, not cotton, farmers. Raw jute is bought at MSP by the Jute Corporation of India. Jute-ICARE stands for Improved Cultivation and Advanced Retting Exercise.

st.2: AP produced about 50 per cent of India's fish in 2024-25.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: AP produced about 30 per cent of India's fish. Statement 4 is incorrect: AP's highest inland fish landings were recorded in 2019-20.

st.4: Vallarpadam (Kerala) and Nanguneri (Tamil Nadu) are examples of National Investment and Manufacturing Zones.
st.1: The SEZ Act, 2005 came into force on 10 February 2005.
st.2: As on 31 March 2025, 268 SEZs were notified and 176 were operational.

x: None of the statements is correct. The SEZ Act came into force on 10 February 2006. On 31 March 2025, 368 SEZs were notified and 276 operational. Tamil Nadu, not Maharashtra, has the most operational SEZs. Vallarpadam and Nanguneri are SEZs, not NIMZs.

st.3: Its Ramachandrapuram unit is in Visakhapatnam.
st.1: Its Bhopal unit is associated with high-pressure boilers.
st.2: Its Jhansi unit makes steam turbines.

x: None of the statements is correct. The Bhopal unit makes heavy electricals and traction motors; boilers are made at Tiruchirappalli. The Jhansi unit makes electric locomotives (transformers), not turbines. Ramachandrapuram is in Hyderabad. Pinjore and Srinagar are HMT units, not BHEL units.

st.2: The CBIC node of Andhra Pradesh is Krishnapatnam in Nellore district.

x: All three statements are correct. AP has nodes on VCIC, CBIC and HBIC; Krishnapatnam is the CBIC node (Orvakal is on HBIC); and Kopparthy, Krishnapatnam and Orvakal are NICDIT-funded.

st.3: The Panama Canal shortens the New York–San Francisco sea distance by about 13,000 km.

x: All three statements are correct. The Suez Canal (1869) is a lockless sea-level canal, the Panama Canal (1914) uses locks to join the Atlantic and Pacific, and it cuts the New York–San Francisco voyage by about 13,000 km.

st.3: Dholavira is India's only Harappan World Heritage Site.

x: All three statements are correct. The Maratha Military Landscapes have 12 forts (11 in Maharashtra plus Gingee), Khangchendzonga is India's only mixed site, and Dholavira is the only Harappan WHS (Lothal is on the tentative list).

st.3: Velland was the first fully computer-literate panchayat.

x: All three statements are correct. Kottayam was the first fully literate town (1989), Ernakulam the first totally literate district (1990), and Velland (Vellanad) the first fully computer-literate panchayat.

st.1: The title of HDR 2016 is 'Human Development for Everyone'.

x: All three statements are correct. 'Human Development for Everyone' was the 2016 HDR title, the HDR was conceived by Mahbub ul Haq, and Amartya Sen won the Economics Nobel in 1998.

st.1: The demographic window opens at the same time in all States.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the window opens at different times in different States. Statement 2 is incorrect: according to the RBI, Bihar and Uttar Pradesh have not yet crossed the turning point.

st.3: West Godavari had the highest female literacy among the 13 districts in 2011.

x: All three statements are correct. Alluri Sitarama Raju is the least literate district (44.67%), ST literacy is about 48.8%, and West Godavari led female literacy in 2011, ahead of Krishna.

st.1: India's total number of PVTGs stands at 75.

x: All three statements are correct. India has 75 PVTGs, the Konda Savara live mainly in the Srikakulam hills, and a declining or stagnant population is a PVTG criterion.

st.3: The Bhotia are the largest Scheduled Tribe of Uttarakhand.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the Bhils, though the largest tribe, form only about a sixth of India's ST population. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Tharu, not the Bhotia, are Uttarakhand's largest ST.

st.3: Indravati is in Chhattisgarh.

x: All three statements are correct. National Chambal Sanctuary spans MP, Rajasthan and UP, Ghatigaon is in Gwalior, and Indravati is in Chhattisgarh.

st.2: Rajiv Gandhi (Rameswaram) NP lies on the north bank of the Penna in Kadapa district.

x: All three statements are correct. Rajiv Gandhi (Rameswaram) NP, AP's smallest national park, lies on the north bank of the Penna in Kadapa and was declared in 2005.

st.1: R. Chidambaram was India's first Principal Scientific Adviser.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: A.P.J. Abdul Kalam was the first PSA (1999); Chidambaram came later. Statement 2 is incorrect: PM-STIAC is chaired by the PSA.

st.2: The Economic Survey 2025-26 recommends that India focus on small, application-specific models rather than large general-purpose frontier models.

x: All three statements are correct. GERD is about 0.64–0.70% of GDP, the Economic Survey 2025-26 favours small, application-specific models, and the Supreme Court sought the Centre's reply on high-risk AI in welfare delivery (August 2026).

st.3: NPE 2019 targets US$ 400 billion of electronics manufacturing and 1 billion mobile handsets a year by 2030.
st.2: MPMS is run by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: MPMS is a MeitY scheme that replaces the PLI for Large Scale Electronics. Statement 3 is incorrect: the NPE 2019 targets are for 2025. Statement 4 is incorrect: MPMS targets production of ₹39 lakh crore (₹15 lakh crore is the export target).

st.3: India's adaptation spending fell from 5.6% of GDP in FY16 to 3.7% in FY22.
st.1: It was prepared under the PM's Council on Climate Change, formed in 2009.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the PM's Council on Climate Change was formed in 2007 (NAPCC came in 2008). Statement 2 is incorrect: four of the eight missions focus on adaptation. Statement 3 is incorrect: adaptation spending rose from 3.7% (FY16) to 5.6% (FY22).

st.2: Curd making is an example of modern biotechnology.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: curd making is traditional biotechnology. Statement 3 is incorrect: the earliest biotechnologists were farmers and food makers, not chemists.

st.1: It is a winged, reusable vehicle aimed at a Single-Stage-To-Orbit (SSTO) system.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: RLV-TD is aimed at a Two-Stage-To-Orbit system. Statement 3 is incorrect: it does need a thermal protection system for re-entry.

st.1: It is a single-engine Advanced Light Helicopter made by HAL.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: Dhruv is a twin-engine helicopter. Statement 2 is incorrect: it is used by the Army, Navy, Air Force and Coast Guard.

st.3: eCourts and e-Procurement are State MMPs.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: e-Panchayat is a State MMP. Statement 3 is incorrect: eCourts and e-Procurement are Integrated MMPs.

st.1: AP Fibernet, offering IPTV, internet and telephone over GPON, was launched on 27 December 2019.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: AP Fibernet was launched on 27 December 2017. Statement 2 is incorrect: it was a Singapore delegation that studied the RTGS Data Lake.

st.2: There were about 5.97 lakh Common Service Centres in April 2025.

x: All three statements are correct. BharatNet covered 2,18,347 GPs by March 2025, there were about 5.97 lakh CSCs, and electronics production rose from Rs 2.13 to Rs 5.25 lakh crore.

st.4: High tariffs, not poor storage or slow transmission, cause regional imbalances in renewable power.
st.2: Delhi has responded to the evening peak by abolishing Time-of-Day tariffs.
st.1: India's record peak demand of 270.8 GW (May 2026) was about 30 GW above 2019.

x: None of the statements is correct. The 270.8 GW peak was about 90 GW above 2019. Delhi introduced, not abolished, Time-of-Day tariffs with smart meters. AT&C losses fell to about 15.04% in FY25. Regional renewable imbalances come from poor storage and slow transmission.

st.2: Diesel prices were deregulated in October 2014.

x: All three statements are correct. Petrol was deregulated in June 2010, diesel in October 2014, and PAHAL (2015) pays the LPG subsidy by DBT.

st.2: 100% FDI is allowed under the automatic route for biofuel technology for export as well as domestic use.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: 100% automatic-route FDI is allowed only where the biofuels are for domestic use. Statement 3 is incorrect: maize-based ethanol is priced above rice- and molasses-based ethanol.

st.1: The decision was taken in 2018.
st.2: Urgent air pollution in Mumbai was one reason.

x: None of the statements is correct. The decision to skip BS-V was taken in 2016. Delhi-NCR's air pollution, not Mumbai's, was a key reason. BS-V was never enforced in any city.

st.2: Odisha has the largest total coal resources among the States.

x: All three statements are correct. Coal resources were 400.715 billion tonnes on 1 April 2025, Odisha has the largest total resources (Jharkhand leads in proved reserves), and India is the second-largest producer.

st.2: Small-hydro potential is 21,133 MW at 7,133 sites.

x: All three statements are correct. India is 3rd in large dams, small-hydro potential is 21,133 MW at 7,133 sites, and installed large hydro is about 51.96 GW.

st.3: Since 2023 Karnataka has been the largest wind State, with Tamil Nadu second.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: India ranks fourth in installed wind capacity. Statement 3 is incorrect: since 2023 Gujarat, not Karnataka, has led, with Tamil Nadu second.

st.1: The niche is the physical address (location) of a species in its habitat.
st.4: Competing species can never coexist on a shared resource.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the niche is a species' functional role ('profession'); its address is the habitat. Statement 2 is incorrect: that describes the fundamental niche, not the realised niche. Statement 4 is incorrect: competitors can coexist by partitioning a shared resource.

st.3: A city is an example of a natural ecosystem.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: a wetland is a natural aquatic ecosystem, not a terrestrial one. Statement 3 is incorrect: a city is an extreme example of an artificial ecosystem.

st.2: Protists are unicellular eukaryotes.

x: All three statements are correct. Azotobacter fixes nitrogen, protists are unicellular eukaryotes, and cyanobacteria are photosynthetic prokaryotes.

st.2: Bhitarkanika in Odisha is a mangrove National Park.

x: All three statements are correct. ICMAM is at Chennai, Bhitarkanika is a mangrove (not marine) National Park, and A&N and Lakshadweep became India's first Hope Spots in 2013.

st.1: It has 66 sections arranged in 10 chapters.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the Act has 66 sections in 7 chapters. Statement 3 is incorrect: Section 38V(3) was inserted by the 2006 amendment, not 2002.

st.2: COD measures the oxygen needed to oxidise both biodegradable and non-biodegradable organic matter.

x: All three statements are correct. Clean water has BOD below 4 mg/L, COD covers both biodegradable and non-biodegradable matter, and sodium salts are dissolved solids.

st.4: Andhra Pradesh runs 19 CETPs.
st.3: India's first CETP was set up at Ankleshwar, Gujarat.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: Tiruppur is in Tamil Nadu. Statement 3 is incorrect: India's first CETP was at Jeedimetla near Hyderabad. Statement 4 is incorrect: Andhra Pradesh runs 9 CETPs.

st.1: In a linear economy, waste is recycled back into production.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: in a linear economy waste is the end point, not recycled. Statement 3 is incorrect: the circular economy covers all materials and resources, not only carbon and fossil fuels.

st.1: Without the greenhouse effect, the Earth's average temperature would be about −33°C instead of +15°C.
st.2: The atmosphere is relatively opaque to incoming short-wave radiation but transparent to outgoing long-wave radiation.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: without the greenhouse effect the average would be about −18°C (33°C is the warming effect). Statement 2 is incorrect: the atmosphere is transparent to incoming short-wave and opaque to outgoing long-wave radiation. Statement 3 is incorrect: the surface absorbs about 51 units; 35 units are reflected.

st.1: Samudrayaan is ISRO's first manned deep ocean mission, targeting 6,000 m.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: Samudrayaan is run by the Ministry of Earth Sciences (NIOT), not ISRO. Statement 2 is incorrect: its 3-member submersible is Matsya-6000, not Varaha.

st.3: Digitally connected village is one of the themes.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: 'industrially advanced village' is not one of the nine themes. Statement 3 is incorrect: 'digitally connected village' is not a theme; the themes include good governance.

st.2: H5N1 causes bird flu (avian influenza).

x: All three statements are correct. Pigs are an important host for H1N1 swine flu, H5N1 causes bird flu, and the May 2018 Nipah outbreak in Kerala was centred in Kozhikode.

st.4: Noise pollution causes hearing loss but has no effect on blood pressure or sleep.
st.2: IQAir 2025 ranked India the 3rd most polluted country, with PM2.5 of 48.9 µg/m³.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: IQAir 2025 ranked India 6th, not 3rd. Statement 3 is incorrect: the WHO annual PM2.5 guideline is 5 µg/m³. Statement 4 is incorrect: noise also causes hypertension, anxiety and sleep disorders.

st.4: Excess saturated fat lowers blood lipids and cholesterol.
st.3: WHO's REPLACE plan set 2025 as the target to eliminate industrially produced trans fats from the global food supply.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: FSSAI caps trans fat at 2%. Statement 3 is incorrect: REPLACE set 2023 as the target. Statement 4 is incorrect: excess saturated fat raises blood lipids and cholesterol.

st.2: As per the India TB Report 2024, 35.52 lakh TB cases were notified in 2023.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: Ni-kshay Poshan support was raised from Rs 500 to Rs 1,000, not Rs 1,500. Statement 2 is incorrect: 25.52 lakh cases were notified in 2023.

st.1: NP-NCD, earlier called NPCDCS, follows hospital-based opportunistic screening rather than population-based screening.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: NP-NCD follows population-based screening. Statement 3 is incorrect: leprosy is not an NCD; MDT continues under the NLEP.

st.2: SDG target 3.4 seeks to cut premature deaths from non-communicable diseases by one-third.

x: All three statements are correct. Target 3.3 seeks to end AIDS, TB, malaria and NTD epidemics by 2030, target 3.4 a one-third cut in premature NCD deaths, and target 3.1 an MMR below 70.

st.1: NACP Phase V (2021-26) aims at an 80% cut in new HIV infections and AIDS deaths.

x: All three statements are correct. NACP V aims at an 80% cut in new infections and deaths, VCTCs are now ICTCs, and the HIV/AIDS Act 2017 bars discrimination.

st.2: The target is to open 25,000 Jan Aushadhi Kendras by March 2027.

x: All three statements are correct. There were 17,990 Kendras in December 2025, the target is 25,000 by March 2027, and the Clinical Establishments Act has been adopted by only about 11 States and 6 UTs.

st.2: It does not need a line of sight to the reader.

x: All three statements are correct. RFID uses radio waves, needs no line of sight, and FASTag is a passive tag powered by the reader.

st.1: SHAR, Sriharikota was renamed the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre.
st.4: Tessy Thomas became the first Indian woman to win the COSPAR Sarabhai Medal in 2026.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: it was TERLS, Thumba that became VSSC; SHAR is named after Satish Dhawan. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Chandrayaan-2 lander Vikram, not the rover Pragyan, was named after him. Statement 4 is incorrect: the 2026 medal went to Annapurni Subramaniam.

st.1: A digital detox is the compulsive urge to keep checking devices.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: a digital detox is a deliberate break from devices. Statement 3 is incorrect: fear of being without one's phone is nomophobia; FOMO is the fear of missing out.

st.1: They bear the signature of Governor Shaktikanta Das.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the new notes bear Governor Sanjay Malhotra's signature. Statement 2 is incorrect: earlier ₹20 notes remain legal tender.

st.2: The SCO Defence Ministers met at Tashkent in April 2026.
st.4: Kyrgyzstan's currency is the Tenge.
st.1: The first India–China bilateral consultations on the SCO were held on 16–17 March 2026.

x: None of the statements is correct. The consultations were held on 16–17 April 2026. The Defence Ministers met at Bishkek, not Tashkent. Kyrgyzstan's President is Sadyr Japarov (Tokayev is Kazakhstan's). Its currency is the Som; the Tenge is Kazakh.

st.2: COP30 agreed a finance path of USD 1.3 trillion a year for developing countries by 2035.

x: All three statements are correct. COP30 was held at Belém in November 2025 and set a USD 1.3 trillion a year path by 2035, and India announced Panchamrit at COP26, Glasgow.

st.3: India is a founding member of the ADB, which was set up in 1966.

x: All three statements are correct. The ADB approved its first Puducherry project ($139.55 million) in November 2026, it is headquartered at Manila under Masato Kanda, and India is a founding member (1966).

st.2: The EU made commitments in 144 services subsectors and India in 102.

x: All three statements are correct. The EU liberalised 97% of tariff lines and India 92.1%, the EU committed 144 services subsectors and India 102, and India protected dairy, cereals, poultry and soymeal.

st.3: It enters into force after 40 ratifications.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: it opens for signature only after the PABS annex is adopted. Statement 3 is incorrect: it enters into force after 60 ratifications.

st.2: Indonesia joined BRICS in January 2024.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: Indonesia joined in January 2025. Statement 3 is incorrect: Saudi Arabia has not formally confirmed membership.

st.1: It bans social media for children under 15 from 1 January 2026.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the ban takes effect from 1 January 2027. Statement 2 is incorrect: there is no exemption with parental consent.

st.3: It is called the "African Quad".

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: I2U2 focuses on joint investment in water, energy, transport, space, health and food security, not defence. Statement 3 is incorrect: it is called the 'West Asian Quad'.

st.2: India holds the BRICS chair for 2026.

x: All three statements are correct. Tashkent's first IT Park was modelled on STPI, India chairs BRICS in 2026, and Uzbekistan and Liechtenstein are the only doubly landlocked countries.

st.3: Canada became a Dialogue Partner of the Indian Ocean Rim Association.

x: All three statements are correct. DAE signed a Cameco uranium deal for 2027–2035, the two set a US$50 billion trade target for 2030, and Canada became a Dialogue Partner (not a full member) of IORA.

st.4: In 3D printing, PLA is used for water-soluble supports.
st.3: NSAM 2.0 focuses only on defence applications.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: NSAM 2.0 is not limited to defence; it covers commercialisation and IPR among others. Statement 4 is incorrect: PVA, not PLA, is the water-soluble support material.

st.3: Mahe-class vessels are built by Cochin Shipyard.

x: All three statements are correct. The programme has 16 vessels: the Arnala class built by GRSE, Kolkata and the Mahe class by Cochin Shipyard.

st.2: NavIC needs at least seven operational satellites to give positioning services.
st.3: The new-generation NVS satellites carry an indigenous atomic clock and have a 10-year design life.

x: None of the statements is correct. IRNSS-1F stopped positioning but continues broadcast messaging. NavIC needs at least four, not seven, operational satellites. NVS satellites have a 12-year design life.

st.1: The first MILAN was held at Port Blair in 1995.

x: All three statements are correct. MILAN began at Port Blair in 1995, the 13th edition (2026) was inaugurated by Rajnath Singh, and it had a record 74 countries.

st.3: The MTU-1010 edit gives submergence tolerance.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: Pusa DST Rice 1 was developed by ICAR-IARI from MTU-1010. Statement 3 is incorrect: the MTU-1010 edit gives drought and salt tolerance, not submergence tolerance.

st.1: National Coastal Mission 2.0 (2025-26 to 2030-31, ₹767 crore) is a Central Sector Scheme.

x: All three statements are correct. NCM 2.0 is a ₹767 crore Central Sector Scheme for 2025-26 to 2030-31 covering 9 coastal States and 4 UTs, and the Pichavaram study found most mangrove carbon below ground.

st.1: It was held at Baku, Azerbaijan, with the theme 'Taking Action for Nature'.
st.2: Its logo shows the apricot blossom with 23 colours for the 23 targets.

x: None of the statements is correct. CBD COP17 was held at Yerevan, Armenia, not Baku. Its logo shows the Eriwan Blue butterfly. COP18 will be at Quito in 2028, not 2030.

st.3: The National Biodiversity Authority was set up in 2003 under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, with headquarters at New Delhi.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Nagoya Protocol was adopted in 2010 and entered into force in 2014. Statement 3 is incorrect: the NBA is headquartered at Chennai.

st.3: In the Large States category, Maharashtra, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu were the leaders.

x: All three statements are correct. Delhi retained 1st place ahead of Maharashtra and Karnataka, AP was 9th with 52 points, and the Large States leaders were Maharashtra, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

st.3: The GCRMN was set up in 1995 under the IUCN.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: the GCRMN was set up under the International Coral Reef Initiative, not the IUCN. Statement 4 is incorrect: Lakshadweep has atolls and the Andamans fringing reefs.

st.1: It links forests to three dimensions of food security – availability, access and utilisation.
st.2: Fewer than 500 million people depend on forests.

x: None of the statements is correct. The report uses four dimensions, including stability. Over 5 billion people depend on forests. Pollinators account for about 35% of crop production, not 53%.

st.1: India is the top-ranked country worldwide in AI readiness.
st.4: Aadhaar, UPI and DigiLocker are cited as privately owned platforms.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: India is among the 10 best emerging markets, not first worldwide. Statement 3 is incorrect: the share of firms using AI is not higher in India than in the US. Statement 4 is incorrect: Aadhaar, UPI and DigiLocker are cited as Digital Public Infrastructure.

st.3: India holds 3,561 of the 6,311 IRCCs under the Cartagena Protocol, the most of any country.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the Nagoya Protocol was adopted in 2010 and came into force in 2014. Statement 3 is incorrect: IRCCs are issued under the Nagoya Protocol, not the Cartagena Protocol.

st.2: Finland was the happiest country in the 2017 report, in which India was 122nd.
st.1: Denmark was the happiest country in the 2015 report.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: Switzerland topped the 2015 report. Statement 2 is incorrect: Norway topped the 2017 report; Finland first topped in 2018.

st.1: It uses GDP per capita (PPP) as its income measure.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the HDI uses GNI per capita (PPP), not GDP. Statement 2 is incorrect: the dimension indices are combined by a geometric mean.

st.3: The Multidimensional Poverty Index is released by the World Bank with OPHI.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the GII is UNDP's and the Global Gender Gap Report the WEF's. Statement 3 is incorrect: the MPI is released by UNDP with OPHI, not the World Bank.

st.2: The prize was first awarded in 1990, jointly to Nelson Mandela and Anatoly Marchenko.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the prize was first awarded in 1988. Statement 3 is incorrect: Tomoko Akane is from Japan.

st.1: Lionel Messi received the 2026 award for Sports at Madrid, Spain.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the awards are presented at Oviedo, not Madrid. Statement 2 is incorrect: the awards have eight categories.

st.2: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes functions under Article 338.

x: All three statements are correct. Hindi Diwas is 14 September and Article 343 makes Hindi official, the NCSC functions under Article 338 (338A is the NCST), and the Sansad Ratna Awards began in 2010.

st.3: His debut novel Sátántangó (1985) was filmed by István Szabó.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: he was born in 1954 at Gyula, not Budapest. Statement 3 is incorrect: Sátántangó was filmed by Béla Tarr, not István Szabó.

st.2: India finished 5th with 17 medals, and Iran topped the table.

x: All three statements are correct. The 22nd edition was held at Bishkek, India finished 5th with 17 medals while Iran topped the table, and Sujeet Kalkal and Abhimanyu Mandwal won freestyle golds.

st.1: India's Sanju Samson was the Player of the Series of the tournament.

x: All three statements are correct. Sanju Samson was Player of the Series (Sahibzada Farhan was top run-scorer), Farhan scored two centuries in one edition, and Bumrah and Varun Chakravarthy took 14 wickets each.

st.2: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao was launched at Panipat on 24 January 2015.
st.1: The International Day of the Girl Child was first observed on 11 October 2011.

x: None of the statements is correct. The International Day of the Girl Child was first observed on 11 October 2012. Beti Bachao Beti Padhao was launched on 22 January 2015. National Girl Child Day is 24 January, not 11 October.

st.3: It was adopted as the National Song on 24 January 1950.

x: All three statements are correct. Vande Mataram was composed by Bankim Chandra and included in Anandamath (1882), first sung by Tagore at the 1896 session, and adopted as the National Song on 24 January 1950.

st.3: The National School of Drama was set up in 1959.

x: All three statements are correct. IFFI was first held in 1952, Kalakshetra was founded in 1936 by Rukmini Devi Arundale, and the National School of Drama was set up in 1959.

st.4: Andhra Pradesh topped the farmer registry, achieving 110% of its target.
